title: The Purpose of Reproof and the Metaphor of the Tree
english: The reproofs were intended so that from this stillness might come, and that he might work the remainder like a hired laborer. But these things are said again to them as it becomes manifest that God gives tolerance for the sake of repentance, as Paul says: 'Or do you despise his tolerance and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?' (Rom 2:4). For it is said that to be still—meaning to cease from evil and to take up virtue—is clearly shown by the words, 'You sinned, be still,' and by 'The earth feared and he was still when God arose to judgment.' For men, having grasped the notion that God is judge, were still from sinning.

For there is hope in a tree; if it is cut off, even so its shoot shall sprout again and its branch shall by no means fail. Through many things he demonstrates that he did not endure the pains because of worthlessness, as the meaning of the word becomes clear: 'Let this be so by hypothesis: the lashings have been sufficient as it is the time to depart.' For neither are the things of repentance rejected, nor does God, as if the will were unchangeable, punish without measure. For there is a fitness in the souls, even if a great pouring out of punishments occurs; therefore, repentance can come to pass.

And he calls the man a tree, as is also said in many places of the Scriptures: 'Already the axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree not producing a good fruit is cut down and is thrown into the fire' (Matt 3:10). And again: 'Either make the tree good and its fruits good, or make the tree rotten and its fruits rotten' (Luke 6:43). Having set this aside once, we shall not leave it unexamined. For the Savior does not command that one should become a rotten tree or bring forth rotten fruit, but that the state of each one be manifest through their actions, and not to prefer the hypocrisy of this. And there is also another way to understand this: the Jews were saying concerning the Savior: 'By Beelzebub, the ruler of the demons, he casts out...'
